question: A 10-year-old boy is found to have a blood pressure of 128/84 mmHg on three separate occasions over 4 weeks. His height is at the 75th percentile for age. Using standard paediatric criteria, which of the following statements about defining his hypertension status is CORRECT?

answers.text: A BP of 128/84 at age 10 automatically meets adult hypertension criteria and no percentile tables are needed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Paediatric hypertension is defined by age-, sex-, and height-specific percentile tables — NOT by fixed adult cut-offs. Adult thresholds (≥130/80 or ≥140/90 depending on the guideline) are not valid for children below 13 years of age. Normal BP rises throughout childhood; a value normal at age 4 may be abnormal at age 10.

answers.text: Hypertension in children is defined as average systolic or diastolic BP at or above the 95th percentile for age, sex, and height on three or more separate occasions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The standard definition (AAP 2017; IAP guidelines align): hypertension = BP ≥95th percentile for age, sex, and height on ≥3 occasions. Stage 1 hypertension is 95th to 95th + 12 mmHg; Stage 2 is ≥95th + 12 mmHg. Elevated BP (previously prehypertension) is 90th to <95th percentile. For adolescents ≥13 years, adult fixed thresholds (≥130/80) may apply.

answers.text: A single elevated BP reading in a 10-year-old is sufficient to diagnose hypertension if both systolic and diastolic values exceed the 90th percentile

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Paediatric hypertension requires elevated readings on THREE or more separate occasions. A single reading can be due to pain, anxiety, or a wrong cuff size. Confirmation over multiple visits is mandatory before the diagnosis is made and workup initiated.

answers.text: In children under 12 years, only secondary causes of hypertension are recognised; primary hypertension does not occur in this age group

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Primary (essential) hypertension does occur in school-age and adolescent children, particularly those who are overweight/obese. However, the younger the child and the higher the BP, the more likely a secondary cause (renal, endocrine, renovascular). Children under 6 years with any degree of hypertension should always be worked up for secondary causes before labelling as primary.

overallFeedback.feedback: Paediatric BP is defined by percentiles (age + sex + height), not adult fixed numbers. Three separate readings are required. Both systolic and diastolic must be compared against the correct normative table.
Correct. The percentile definition is essential: BP ≥95th percentile for age + sex + height on 3 separate occasions = hypertension. Always use the correct cuff size and age-appropriate tables.
